A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Refusal Index research. All 24 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison through readable text and rendered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on SimpleQA, PreciseWikiQA and FaithEval, including refusal stability, calibration agreement, copula comparisons and sample-size analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a comparison of confidence estimators on Qwen3-32B in Appendix L.

M1.justification: The Spearman-based RI definition, Gaussian-copula estimator and two-pass refusal/forced-answering procedure remain unchanged. The aggregated indicator receives an equivalent algebraic expression, and the Python implementation is identical.

E1.justification: The named datasets and factual-answering/context scenarios remain unchanged. However, new Appendix L uses an unspecified 'mixed factual QA set'; its composition is insufficiently documented to establish whether it introduces different data coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix L newly evaluates the P(IK) linear probe and APRICOT alongside P(Answering), relating their diagnostics to RI. This comparison on one model expands the comparator set; the existing factuality metrics and copula alternatives remain. Verbalized confidence appears only in the descriptive comparison table.

E3.justification: Appendix L introduces a common held-out evaluation of three calibrators using ECE, ten-bin reliability diagrams and ROC/AUROC comparisons. Existing decoding settings, refusal prompts, benchmark procedures and sampling-based AUROC evaluation are retained.

E4.justification: The new Qwen3-32B case study tests whether different confidence estimators produce different calibration diagnoses. Existing copula, sample-size and prompt-agreement analyses remain unchanged. Figure 9 mainly expands visualization of the existing four-prompt evaluations.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same Table 7 confidence intervals using a bootstrap with 1,000 samples, the same 50-subset sample-size analysis and the same regression bands in Figure 4. No new repeated-run, seed or result-uncertainty reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds Gemma-3-12B results, including RI variability of 0.23, and revises averages. Figure 13 newly reports ECE/AUROC pairs of 0.098/0.914 for P(IK), 0.039/0.968 for APRICOT and 0.122/0.939 for P(Answering). Figure 5 changes R² from 0.235 to 0.242, although the discussion retains 0.235. Tables 3, 4, 6 and 7 retain their results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition, copula assumption, likelihood and Appendix E propositions and proofs are retained. Added explanations of latent probabilities, unrestricted marginals and rank measures do not introduce new formal results; the stability formulas describe existing metrics.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain RI, its lightweight two-pass estimator, stability across refusal tendencies, and evidence that factual accuracy does not ensure reliable refusal. The rewritten abstract and introduction preserve these claims and the stated 16-model, five-dataset scope.

C2.justification: Appendix L adds the interpretation that external calibrators can conceal overconfidence, whereas refusal-frequency confidence exposes behavior consistent with moderate RI. Existing interpretations concerning model families, prompting and contextual information remain, as do Appendix A's limitations.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents the formulas for the existing stability summaries and describes the new probe's hidden-state inputs and APRICOT's external-model training on generated reasoning traces. Main prompts, hardware, decoding settings, RI code and availability statements are unchanged. Detailed training settings and data composition for the new comparison remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. The expanded Background and Table 8 develop the comparison with already cited confidence-estimation approaches, emphasizing estimator-dependent calibration, bias and computational cost without fundamentally changing the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially restructures the opening narrative: it condenses the abstract and introduction, moves and expands motivation into a dedicated Background section, presents contributions as bullets, and reframes experimental headings as questions. Method explanations are expanded, and new appendix sections reorganize the supporting narrative.

P2.justification: Visual presentation expands with the six-panel iso-RI Figure 9, calibration Figure 13 and comparison Table 8. Figure 5 is redrawn with individual-model symbols and a full legend; tables receive revised styling and RI highlighting, and several displays move. Existing sample-size, prompt-agreement and implementation figures are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The reorganized motivation, expanded visual evidence and added calibrator comparison make v2's argument easier to assess, while Table 2 reports a broader stability comparison. These are limited gains: Appendix L lacks important dataset and training specifications, and Figure 5 introduces an unresolved 0.242-versus-0.235 discrepancy between the graphic and discussion.
